transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It's, um, it's very nice to meet you. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I'm here because... well, it's a little embarrassing to even say out loud, to be honest. I don't want to come across as difficult or, you know, unprofessional. But things have been really stressful with my work. I do mathematical modeling—environmental datasets, mostly. And lately, I'm pretty sure the people on this one contract have been tracking my revisions. 

I know that probably just sounds like standard oversight, but... I really think they're actively planting errors in the datasets. Just to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. My wife and the junior analysts, they keep telling me it's just normal version-control mistakes, and I really try to listen to them. I don't want to be making a fuss out of nothing. But it just feels so deliberate. Does... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm looking at this the right way, and I'd really value your opinion on it.
How certain are you that this is happening?

Well... I really try to be open-minded about it. I don't want to be stubborn or difficult, you know? So when my wife or the junior analysts tell me it's just normal version-control mistakes, I always listen to them. I really, really want to believe them, because... well, it would be much easier if I was just making a fuss over nothing, wouldn't it? 

But... I've been working with these environmental datasets for a long time. And I'm... I'm pretty certain. I mean, despite what they say, I'm almost positive someone is going in and planting those errors on purpose. The way it's being done, it just feels so calculated to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

I really don't want to sound unreasonable or paranoid, Doctor. I know how that must sound to you. Do you think I'm overreacting by feeling this sure about it? I just want to be a good professional, but it's so hard to ignore when I can see it happening.
Have you had any episodes of feeling unusually depressed or unusually energized or euphoric around the time this started?

Oh, um... no, I don't believe so. I mean, I hope I'm answering that right, but... I haven't felt depressed. And definitely not euphoric or, you know, bouncing off the walls or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a very even keel. I don't want to be a burden on my wife or make things harder at the office by being moody, so I just... I just try to stay steady, you know? Just keep my head down and do my work. So my mood has been pretty normal, all things considered. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Have you had any recent head injury, seizure, or new neurological problem?

Oh, no, definitely not. Nothing like that at all. I haven't hit my head, and I certainly haven't had any seizures or... or anything neurological. 

I've always been very healthy, physically speaking. I make sure to take good care of myself so I don't cause any worry for my family. I haven't even had a headache recently, to be honest. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to be sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to notice?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I mean... my eyes and ears are working just fine, thankfully. I haven't been seeing anything out of the ordinary, or hearing voices or... or anything of that nature. 

I know sometimes people can imagine things when they're under a lot of stress, but I really try to keep a firm grip on reality. I'm just looking at the numbers and the datasets, exactly as they are on the screen. I hope that's a good sign? I really want to be as helpful as possible, Doctor, so please let me know if I'm giving you the answers you need. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything from you, I just... I haven't experienced anything like that.
Aside from this concern about the dataset errors, have you been able to keep up with your work and daily life as usual?

Well, I... I try my absolute best, I really do. I don't want to let anyone down, especially my team. But, um... to be completely honest, and I hope you won't think too poorly of me for this, but I... I have fallen a bit behind on the modeling deliverables. Just a little bit. It got to the point where the firm had to reassign some pieces of the contract, which... well, it's not ideal. And I haven't been quite as available to the junior analysts I'm supposed to supervise. I just... I feel like I haven't been very useful to them lately. 

And at home... well, I mostly just keep to myself these days. My wife, bless her heart, she's been so patient, but she's had to kind of push me just to keep up with the basic daily routines. I really hope I'm not sounding like a complete failure here, Doctor. I'm trying to get back on track, I promise. Does that... is that the kind of information you needed to know?
Do you think the people you believe are targeting you have any extraordinary or implausible power or ability, like controlling your thoughts or causing events from a distance?

Oh, no, definitely nothing like that. I mean, they're just... they're just people, you know? Clever people who know how to manipulate data and ruin a model, but they don't have any sort of... magical powers or anything. 

I certainly don't believe anyone is controlling my thoughts or, or doing anything impossible from far away. I know that sounds completely crazy, and I promise you, I'm very grounded in reality. I'm a numbers guy, Doctor. I deal with logic and statistics. I wouldn't entertain anything so... irrational. 

I just think there are individuals who want to see my work discredited, and they're using normal, albeit underhanded, methods to do it. I hope that makes sense? I really want to assure you that my mind is perfectly sound when it comes to things like that. I'm not... I'm not losing my grip or anything, am I?
Outside of the dataset issue, have you had any other fixed beliefs that other people have said are not true?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I... I really try to be a very reasonable person, Doctor. Aside from the situation at work with the data—which I know probably sounds a bit complicated to an outsider—I don't have any... well, any other unusual ideas or things people tell me are untrue. 

I mean, my wife and I might disagree on small everyday things, just normal married life, but nothing serious or out of the ordinary. I'm a very logical man, really. Just a regular guy who likes his routines and his statistics. I wouldn't hold onto anything that didn't make rational sense. 

I hope that's... I mean, I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers? I just want to assure you that I'm completely level-headed about everything else. I really want to be cooperative here. Does that make sense, Doctor?
How long have you been convinced that the data are being planted?

Well, I... I suppose it's been about two months now. Just the last two months, really. That's when I became certain that... well, that people on the project were tracking my revisions and, um, planting those errors. 

I know two months might sound like a while to be worried about something like this, but I really did try to just ignore it at first. I didn't want to make a fuss or seem difficult to work with. I always try to be a team player. But the evidence just kept piling up in the models, and... well, I couldn't just look the other way anymore. 

It's only been two months, though. Before that, everything was perfectly fine. I hope you don't think less of me for letting it get to me for this long. I really am trying to handle it professionally. Is that... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for, Doctor?
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t, at any time in your life?

Oh, goodness, no. Never anything like that. I... I know that's something psychiatrists always have to ask about, but I promise you, I've never heard voices or seen visions or anything of the sort. 

I'm a very grounded person, Doctor. Like I said, I work with numbers all day. My brain just isn't wired for... well, for hallucinations or anything that isn't strictly factual. I've always had a very firm grasp on reality, my whole life. 

I hope you believe me. I know I've been very stressed about the situation at work, but it hasn't caused anything like that. I'm completely normal in that regard. I'm doing okay, aren't I? I mean, my answers are showing that I'm still thinking clearly?
Have you been convinced that people are targeting the data for at least one month?

Yes, yes, definitely. Like I mentioned just a moment ago, it's been about two months now that I've been... well, certain about the errors being planted and the revisions being tracked. 

So, yes, it has been at least a month. I... I hope it's okay that I brought it up again. I know I already said two months, but I just want to make sure I'm answering your question exactly how you need me to. I'm trying to be as precise as possible for you, Doctor. I know how important accuracy is. Am I... am I giving you the right details?
Have these beliefs about the data being planted been going on for at least six months?

Oh, no, no, not six months. Definitely not that long. As I... as I think I mentioned before, it's really just been the last two months that I've been completely certain about them tracking my revisions and, you know, planting those errors in the data. 

Before that, everything was running quite smoothly. I wouldn't want you to think this has been some long, drawn-out issue that I've been letting fester. I'm usually very quick to resolve workplace conflicts, I promise. It's just been these last two months that things got so... undeniable. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, Doctor. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact timeline you need. I am being helpful, aren't I?
Have you had this belief that the data are being planted continuously for six months or longer?

No, Doctor, not six months. I... I know you just asked that, and I hope it's alright that I'm just confirming it again. I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes. 

It really has just been about the last two months that I've had this... this certainty that people on the project are tracking my revisions and planting those errors. Before that, everything was fine. I wouldn't want you to think I've been struggling with this for half a year without saying anything. I try to be very on top of things, very professional. 

So, just two months. Is... is that the kind of specific timeframe you were looking for? I just want to be sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions.
During these two months, have you mostly been able to function normally at work and at home, or has this belief caused a marked decline in your functioning?

Well, I... I wouldn't say it's been a *marked* decline, exactly. I mean, I'm still going in, I'm still trying my best. I just... I suppose things have been a little more challenging than usual. 

I did fall a bit behind on some of the modeling deliverables. Just a little bit. And, well, the firm did reassign some pieces of the contract to other people, but I think that was just to help me out, you know? To lighten the load. And I haven't been quite as available to the junior analysts I supervise, but they're very capable, they don't need me hovering over them all the time. 

At home... well, my wife has been very supportive. She's had to remind me to keep up with some basic routines, and I've been keeping to myself a bit more, just to focus. But it's nothing too severe, I promise. I'm still managing. I hope that doesn't sound too bad, Doctor. I really am trying my hardest to keep everything on track. Is... is that okay? Am I explaining that alright?
Do you believe these data errors are being planted in a way that requires someone to be physically present at your computer or workplace?

Oh, no, no, they wouldn't need to be physically at my desk. I mean, we're all very connected on the network, so it's quite easy to access files remotely. I wouldn't want you to think I believe people are sneaking into my office or anything like that. That would sound a bit... well, a bit silly, wouldn't it? 

It's all done digitally. They can just slip into the shared drives and alter the code or the datasets without ever having to leave their own workstations. It's very sophisticated, really. I just... I try to keep an eye on the version histories, but they're quite clever about it. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining the technical side of it clearly enough. I don't want to sound like I'm making wild accusations about people breaking into my workspace. I'm being reasonable about this, aren't I?
Have you had any of these beliefs or related unusual experiences continuously for six months or longer?

No, Doctor, not six months. I... I know you just asked that earlier, and I hope it's alright that I'm just confirming it again. I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes. 

It really has just been about the last two months that I've had this... this certainty about the project data. Before that, everything was perfectly fine. I wouldn't want you to think I've been struggling with this for half a year without saying anything. I try to be very on top of things, very professional. 

So, just two months. Is... is that the kind of specific timeframe you were looking for? I just want to be sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions.
Have you become much more emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to be?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I'm completely flat, Doctor. I still care about things, I really do. It's just... maybe I've been a bit more quiet lately? 

I used to love going out, you know. I'd go hiking, or I'd take my telescope out for the local astronomy nights. I really enjoyed mentoring the younger analysts at the firm, too. But lately... I don't know, I just haven't felt the same pull to do those things. 

Sometimes I'll just sit at my desk for hours, or I'll go out to the garage and just sit there with the telescope still covered up. It's not that I'm sad, exactly. I just... I don't really feel the urge to start a project or talk to anyone. I suppose I'm just conserving my energy, really. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound cold or uncaring. I still value my hobbies and my colleagues, I just... I need a bit more downtime right now. Is that fairly normal, Doctor? To just need a break from being so expressive all the time? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression.
Have you ever had anything like this happen before, even if it was less intense or didn’t last as long?

No, Doctor, nothing like this. I mean, I've always been very level-headed, very rational. In my line of work, you have to be. Numbers and data, they don't really leave room for... well, for getting carried away with things. 

I've never had any sort of trouble like this in the past. I've always been a very reliable employee, a good colleague. I wouldn't want you to think I have a history of... of making a fuss or letting my imagination run wild. This is very out of the ordinary for me, I assure you. 

I hope that's a good thing, that it's never happened before? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of my background. I've always been very steady, really.
Have you been convinced that the data are being planted for at least one month?

Yes, Doctor. I... I know I mentioned the timeframe just a moment ago, so I hope it's alright that I'm repeating it. I really just want to make sure I'm being as accurate as possible for you. 

But yes, to answer your question directly... it's been about two months now. That's how long I've had this... this certainty that the people on the project are tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the data. 

I tried not to jump to conclusions at first, because I really don't want to be the kind of person who points fingers or causes trouble at work. I always try to keep things pleasant and professional with the team. But yes, it's been going on for about the last two months. 

Does that give you the right timeline for your notes? I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you're asking for.
Have your thoughts ever felt jumbled or hard to follow, so that other people have trouble understanding what you mean?

Oh, no, Doctor. I... I wouldn't say that at all. I've always prided myself on being very articulate, actually. 

In my line of work, dealing with mathematics and data analysis all day, you really have to be precise. A jumbled thought could ruin a whole report, you know? So I always try to lay things out very logically and clearly for people. I don't think my colleagues or anyone else has ever had trouble following what I mean. I always do my best to make sure I'm not causing any confusion.

I... I hope I've been making sense to you today? I'd hate to think I was rambling or being difficult to understand. Am I communicating clearly enough for your assessment? I just want to make sure I'm giving you good, helpful answers.
